GEAR / MERINO WOOL

A warmer start. A better base.

Merino for fishing, without the guesswork: fabric weights, fit, care, and a few useful picks for cool mornings.

Castward field notes Updated 11 November 2026

Quick answer

Smartwool is my pick for the best 100% merino wool brand. Its Classic Thermal crew has 250 g/m² fabric and flatlock seams for a warm base layer. Check the label: other Smartwool lines use blends.[1]

01

Merino, synthetic, or cotton?

A favorite synthetic base is still useful. Choose the fabric that suits your trip and feels good against your skin.[9] [10]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

FabricWhat it does wellWhere to be careful
Merino woolSoft feel and odor resistanceNeeds gentle care; thin fabric can wear at friction points.
SyntheticQuick drying and easy careOdor performance varies by fabric and finish.
CottonComfort for a dry, mild dayHolds water; a poor choice for a cold, wet base layer.
02

Two numbers. Two different jobs.

Microns measure fiber diameter; smaller fibers generally feel softer. Grams per square metre (g/m², or gsm) measure fabric weight, not a guaranteed temperature range.[10] [2] [3] [4]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

Use suggestions, based on Icebreaker’s weight categories. Wind, rain, activity, and personal comfort change the choice.
Fabric weightStart here forLayering note
120–150 gsmHigh effort or milder daysCarry warmth for stops.
About 200 gsmMixed activity in cool weatherA useful middle starting point.
240–260 gsmSlower, colder outingsCheck that your shell and waders still fit.
320+ gsmVery low activity in cold conditionsMore fabric is not a substitute for a full system.
A useful micron comparison

MERIWOOL lists 18.5 microns for its 250 crew. Icebreaker lists 18.9 microns for the 200 Oasis. Try the fabric if wool makes you itch.

03

Pure wool or a blend?

Read the full fiber label. A wool percentage alone does not tell you how the seams, fit, or high-wear areas will hold up.[1] [3]

What works well

  • 100% merino makes the fiber choice simple.
  • Nylon or other fibers can reinforce a blend; elastane can add stretch.

The trade-offs

  • Pure wool does not guarantee a tougher garment.
  • A blend’s performance depends on its fiber mix and construction.
04

Check the fit before the forecast

  1. 01

    Match the body chart

    Measure your chest for tops and waist or hips for bottoms. Use the exact brand and fit chart.

  2. 02

    Move as you would fish

    Reach forward, lift your arms, and squat. The fabric should stay close without pulling at seams.

  3. 03

    Try the full system

    Put your fleece, shell, socks, and waders over it. Check cuffs and waistbands for pressure.

A size is not shared across brands

For example, Smartwool’s men’s top chart lists Medium at a 38–40 inch chest. Check the current chart for the garment you buy.

[1] [3]
05

What the wool labels mean

Check the exact product claim. A certification on one collection does not cover everything in the shop.[11] [12]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

LabelWhat to look forWhat it does not tell you
RWSAnimal-welfare, land-management and supply-chain requirements; mulesing is prohibited.Garment warmth or service life.
ZQA grower standard with animal-welfare and traceability requirements; mulesing is prohibited from entry.That every item from a brand uses certified wool.
Mulesing-free claimA claim about one animal-management practice. Ask for traceable evidence.A full, independent sustainability certification.
Read the current standard

RWS allows limited, approved restocking with mulesed sheep. Their wool cannot be sold as RWS certified and must stay separate.

06

Care guide: keep the good feel

  1. 01

    Air it after use

    Let the base layer dry fully after your trip. Wash when it needs cleaning.

  2. 02

    Read the actual label

    The Oasis label says cold gentle wash and no softener. Smartwool’s listed Thermal Crew permits a warm gentle wash.

  3. 03

    Use the right drying method

    Oasis says line dry in shade, with no tumble dryer. The listed Smartwool Crew permits tumble dry on low.

  4. 04

    Store it clean and dry

    Keep wool away from damp storage and pests. Inspect cuffs, elbows, and seams before a long trip.

How long will it last?

There is no useful universal year count. Watch for thinning fabric, small holes, and worn seams; mend small damage before it spreads.

08

Read the guarantee with the receipt

A guarantee describes a remedy, not the expected life of the garment. Keep your receipt and check the seller before you order.[7] [8]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

BrandThe stated promiseCheck before you buy

A few good questions

Before you head out

Is 100% merino always better?

No. A blend may suit the job better. Compare the fiber mix, seams, fit, and care instructions.

Can merino replace a fleece?

A base layer and a fleece do different jobs. Add insulation when your activity and conditions call for it.

Does a premium base layer mean more warmth?

No. Compare fabric weight and construction first. The 200 Oasis is lighter than the 250 gsm crews here.
